open.said: This is the weekly call for November fourteenth to twentieth. Three hundred and ten pull requests merged across both repositories, ninety-one of them home's release moving forward, and forty-seven fixed a defect. It was a week of interview practice, Rust Rounds and the phone's link to home.

gray.title: An old WebView always reaches its update page
gray.said: OWV1 now holds that a phone whose WebView is too old for the app gets the page telling it what to update, however the app is opened, cold or warm.

gray.title: The phone knows every feed home renders
gray.said: FEED8 now holds that the phone recognises each feed home renders, the engagement report's included, instead of showing one it doesn't know as broken.

gray.title: What counted comes from home's own record
gray.said: RR30 now holds that Rust Rounds and the interview week say what counted from home's own record, not from what the phone remembers sending.

gray.title: The teleprompter never jumps back by itself
gray.said: PB1 now holds that the teleprompter band never moves the script back on its own, whatever happens when a take ends or you pause.

gray.title: The compatibility storm checks what it promises
gray.said: CS1 now holds that the Android compatibility storm checks the refresh promises as they're written, whether a pull is still running or has ended.

gray.title: Home answers within eight seconds
gray.said: AD4 now holds that home answers every request within eight seconds, saying it's busy rather than going silent, and that a write that can't get a database connection in time says busy too.

gray.title: A pull never waits past its deadline
gray.said: HERD2 now holds that nothing a pull waits on outlives its deadline, that a pull re-reads every screen that reads home, and that home's overload reads as busy.

gray.title: A take stops when you leave the page
gray.said: VC4 now holds that a take stops playing, and a recording ends, when the phone leaves the page, whatever state the take was in.

gray.title: The interview routine runs on a fresh clone
gray.said: IWR1 now holds that the interview week's Monday routine sets itself up on a fresh, shallow clone.

gray.title: Each home's busy is its own
gray.said: AD3 now holds that every request you send, and the check, start home's busy period, and that each home you've paired keeps its own.

gray.title: Pairing again keeps what the phone knows
gray.said: MP1 now holds that pairing again with the same home and account keeps the phone's memory of what home holds, even after a reinstall from a backup.

gray.title: What counts is what you send
gray.said: IWC1 now holds that the interview's words say what you send counts, in every word on those pages, not what home has.

gray.title: A long scene of the call is paged
gray.said: CF1 now holds that a scene of this call too long for its frame is paged, never cut off, whatever the list's length and the text.

gray.title: The recorder only opens pages the stage has
gray.said: RI2 now holds that a recorder fails its test if it opens a page the render stage doesn't carry.

gray.title: A pull stays within home's limit
gray.said: HERD1 now holds that a pull, and everything beside it, stays within home's rate limit across reloads, whatever the order and speed of requests.

gray.title: A pull keeps its backoff
gray.said: AW1 was amended so that a pull keeps the backoff it had when the network changes.

gray.title: A refresh cut short goes on when you're back
gray.said: HERD4 now holds that a refresh cut short by leaving the app finishes once the app is back in front.

gray.title: An essay scene too big for the frame is refused
gray.said: EF1 now holds that finishing an essay refuses a scene the frame can't hold, naming it, and that each point is judged from its own take.

gray.title: Every part of the call gets chapters
gray.said: SFEED4 now holds that every part of the call gets chapters, even a part inside a single section.

gray.title: The public site keeps nothing a visitor writes
gray.said: VS1 now holds that the public site keeps nothing a visitor writes across a reload, whatever the build settings and how storage is imported.

gray.title: A take home couldn't make out is unanswered
gray.said: EH1 now holds that the essays treat a take home couldn't make out as unanswered, never waiting on it.

gray.title: Your habit tracker shows home's history
gray.said: AR1 now holds that your habit tracker shows home's history as its screens open, beside what it is still sending.

gray.title: The recorder asks the speaker in bounded parts
gray.said: SPK1 now holds that the recorder asks home's speaker in bounded pieces, so a long scene or a slow speaker can't stall a recording.

gray.title: A refused render says why
gray.said: RNR1 now holds that a render home's policy refused says why, on every feed, instead of 'Burnt'.

gray.title: A read of home waits for the pairing
gray.said: PO1 now holds that anything reading home as a page opens waits for the pairing record, and says nothing about having no pairing until it's read.

gray.title: The screenshot workflow builds what it imports
gray.said: SN1 now holds that the screenshot bundle job builds the package its script imports before it runs.

gray.title: The web's pairing code points at real pages
gray.said: PW1 now holds that the pairing code on the web points at the phone's real pages, through renames of the page or its button.

gray.title: A paired phone's session renews while you use it
gray.said: RN1 now holds that a paired phone's session is renewed each time the app comes to the front.

gray.title: What home holds counts under the pairing that said it
gray.said: HP1 now holds that what the phone believes home holds counts only under the pairing that said so, through unpairing and pairing changes.

gray.title: The video palette tests get time to run
gray.said: VP1 now holds that the video palette's encoding tests get a thirty-second bound, so a loaded machine doesn't fail them.

gray.title: A network failure is named as itself
gray.said: NA1 now holds that a name not found or an untrusted certificate is reported as itself, never as something vaguer.

gray.title: A cheat sheet is laid out once
gray.said: BIT1 now holds that the cheat-sheet card lays each sheet out once, whatever the machine's load.

gray.title: The phone catches up after home restarts
gray.said: HR1 now holds that the phone catches up after home restarts, however long the restart takes.

gray.title: The phone waits as home asks
gray.said: HR2 now holds that the phone waits as long as home asks after an overload or 'too many requests', without repeating in between.

gray.title: A busy read says the phone was busy
gray.said: RO1 now holds that a read that stays busy says this phone was busy with home, not that home was unreachable.

gray.title: Monday reads each point's own takes
gray.said: PN1 now holds that Monday's pull fetches the transcripts of each point's own takes.

gray.title: Commit trailers read longer promise names
gray.said: TR1 now holds that a commit trailer reads a promise name of up to eight letters.

gray.title: The phone's log keeps the whole cause
gray.said: NL1 now holds that the phone's log keeps a failure's whole chain of causes.

gray.title: The signing workflow treats its input as data
gray.said: WS1 now holds that the manual signing workflow uses the extension it's given only as data, never as code.

gray.title: The render image builds what the stage imports
gray.said: RI3 now holds that the render image is built from what its stage actually imports, and built on every pull request.

gray.title: The recorder's imports are in the image
gray.said: RI1 now holds that everything the recorder imports, directly or not, is in the render image.

gray.title: A badge counts as seen once revealed
gray.said: BS1 now holds that a status badge counts as seen once its reveal ends inside the scene.

gray.title: Renders says why the policy refused
gray.said: RF2 now holds that the render board says which policy refused an episode, and how.

gray.title: A refused render waits for a change
gray.said: RF1 now holds that a refused render is held until its input, its caps or the render image change, instead of retried on a clock.

gray.title: Home takes a corrected week while it has no video
gray.said: CW3 now holds that home takes in a newer revision of a week it holds only while no part of that week has a video.

mine.title: Korean word sets are archived only by you
mine.said: A Korean word set leaves Read aloud only when you archive it from My data. Sets unopened for a month are marked as a hint. An agent chose this alone, because the phone only knows when a set was first opened, so an automatic rule could pull lines you're still drilling.
options: You archive, with a hint
Archive after a set goes unused
Archive when the fifty fill
mine.why: The phone records a set's first open, not its last use, so an automatic rule could remove sets still in use.
mine.undo: Add an automatic archive rule and drop the Archive control.

mine.title: The pickup landed with a known gap
mine.said: A Studio take you move off ready for pickup before the daily run can still be filed as an issue, and you'd close the stray one. An agent landed the pickup with that gap stated rather than wait for the fix. That was Claude's call, under your go-with-the-recommended.
options: Land now, you close a stray issue
First have home withdraw a pickup, then land
mine.why: Whether a day's window for a stray filing is acceptable is a product choice no check settles.
mine.undo: Build the withdrawal, so a run files a pickup only while it's the take's newest move.

mine.title: At most sixteen phones per account
mine.said: Paired phones now have their own cap of sixteen per account. A seventeenth pairing is refused, and no phone is ever evicted to make room. You'd said to keep phone pairings past thirty-two, but named no number; the agent picked sixteen alone.
options: A separate cap of sixteen, refused past it
No cap on phones
Phones share the cap of thirty-two
mine.why: You named no bound, an uncapped table breaks home's bounded rows, and evicting a phone is the failure this removed.
mine.undo: Change the phone cap, or drop the count when a phone pairs.

mine.title: A pull sends at most twenty requests at once
mine.said: The phone now lets twenty requests to home go at once, down from forty-nine, and remembers what's left across page loads, so reopening the app doesn't hand it a fresh burst. A big refresh finishes a little slower. Claude's call alone.
options: Twenty, kept across page loads
Forty-nine, kept across page loads
Ten, kept across page loads
Whatever home says its limit is
mine.why: Home's real limit is a secret, so no check settles the burst; you'd notice a slow pull or a refused one.
mine.undo: Change the burst size, or stop remembering it across page loads.

mine.title: An old WebView gets a plain update page
mine.said: A phone with a WebView older than the app needs gets a plain page instead of the app, saying to update Android System WebView or Chrome, with a button to each in the Play Store. You approved the screen; its words, links and how an old WebView is spotted were Claude's.
options: Capacitor's own check, with a static page
A script reading the browser version
The words alone, with no link
mine.why: You approved the screen but not its words, its link, or how an old WebView is recognised.
mine.undo: Remove the minimum WebView version and the page from the app's config.

mine.title: Notes on new feeds stay on home
mine.said: Home now keeps a note on any feed's episode, but only notes on the weekly call and Playoff Delta go on to the daily run, as before. Notes on the other feeds stay home, since that path is being retired. Claude's call alone.
options: File every feed's note
Widen the mailbox and the routine to every feed
Keep other feeds' notes on home only
mine.why: The mailbox refuses other feeds' notes, and you'd said no routine files notes from now on; whether an essay's note reaches the old routine is something you'd notice.
mine.undo: Widen which feeds' notes go to the mailbox, once the mailbox accepts them.

mine.title: Home finds your issues by public search
mine.said: To show which issue a take became, home runs two public GitHub searches every fifteen minutes over your own issues and pull requests. You chose public search with no key; how often and how wide were Claude's.
options: Two searches of your own items every fifteen minutes
A search per take
A search per repository
Any author's items
mine.why: You named public search with no key, but no freshness or scope.
mine.undo: Change the query or the interval in home's search pass.

mine.title: The teleprompter starts at 170 words a minute
mine.said: You found 140 words a minute too slow, so the teleprompter now starts at 170, with Slower and Faster buttons under it, in steps of 20, and it remembers your pace. The number, the step and where the buttons sit were Claude's.
options: 170, with Slower and Faster, kept on the phone
A faster fixed pace
Each card's own target pace
A slider in Settings
mine.why: You asked for faster and a simple control, but no check settles the number, the step or the place.
mine.undo: Change the default pace or the step, or remove the buttons.

mine.title: Both essays share a sixty-minute cap
mine.said: The Rust Rounds and interview essays now share one length cap of sixty minutes, so a full interview week of three-minute takes fits. You'd said limits like these are suggestions; the number was Claude's.
options: Both share sixty minutes
Rust Rounds thirty, interview fifteen
No length cap, size caps only
mine.why: You treat duration limits as suggestions but named no number.
mine.undo: Set the shared cap back to thirty and give the interview essay its own.

mine.title: A middle interview take keeps its row
mine.said: When home lets go of a middle interview take's recording at week's end, My data keeps its row with what home heard, says when the recording went, and still plays a copy if this phone has one. Claude's call alone.
options: Keep the row, and a copy here still plays
Keep the row, with no Play
Drop the row, leaving only a receipt
mine.why: How My data shows a recording let go by rule rather than by you, and whether the phone's copy still plays.
mine.undo: Drop the line and play from home only.

mine.title: Home keeps each week's engagement report as a record
mine.said: Home keeps each ended week's engagement report once, in a record that leaves with your account, and writes the render's file from it. That's what My data says deleting your account erases. Claude's call, under your go-with-the-recommended.
options: A record on home, the file its copy
The file alone
No record, read the week again
mine.why: The file alone outlives the account, and re-reading a week breaks the same records giving the same video.
mine.undo: Drop the record and write the weekly read straight to the drive, after a durable copy.

mine.title: One interview question a day
mine.said: The interview week now asks one question a day, in order and round again, with nothing carried over, so a day left alone leaves no trace. The week's other questions are one tap away. Claude proposed it and you agreed.
options: One a day, nothing carried over
Two a day
One a day, yesterday's carried over
mine.why: How much the day asks of you, for a skill you avoid; a carried-over question is a quiet mark of a missed day.
mine.undo: Make it two a day, or hold a question until a take answers it.

mine.title: The tappable card's look, chosen by blind judges
mine.said: Among three looks that each met your rule for tappable cards, three fresh judges given only screenshots ranked the elevated card first, and all three ranked the old glow last. Claude chose it on that, and you agreed.
options: Elevated: hairline and a soft shadow
Outlined: hairline only
Tonal: hairline on a muted surface
mine.why: Each variant met the floor and ceiling; which reads best is a judgement.
mine.undo: Swap the card link's look for the outlined or tonal one.

asks.question: Cleaning the noisy recorded video: Auphonic, or keep the footage on home?
asks.said: Filed today. A noisy recorded video could be cleaned now by Auphonic, with the music bed as a ducked second track, but that needs your account and sends your footage to a third party. Keeping it home means folding a denoiser into home's render first. The recommendation is to try Auphonic and say what it got wrong.
asks.whyYours: It needs your account, and it sends your footage to a third party.

options.says: Try Auphonic with the music bed as a ducked second track, and tell me what it got wrong
options.unblocks: A clean video now, and the evidence any later build would rest on
Folding a denoiser into home's render, one worker session

asks.question: When the phone can't tell how much storage it uses, refuse a save, or count a cautious figure?
asks.said: Sometimes the phone can't tell how much browser storage it's using. It could refuse the save and say so, or count a cautious figure and let the save through. It's about your own record, so it's yours. The recommendation is the cautious figure, so no save is refused for this.
asks.whyYours: It trades a save refused now against a backup that may later leave things out: a call about your own record, not a code one.

options.says: Count a cautious figure (say, the most the browser storage has ever used) and let the save through, with a note in This phone
options.unblocks: #3159 with no save ever refused for this reason

options.says: Refuse the save and say the phone couldn't check its room

asks.question: After home says it's overloaded, should the phone stay slower for a day?
asks.said: Right now, when home says it's overloaded, the phone keeps sending more slowly for a day. The recommendation is to wait as home asks and then go back to the usual pace, keeping the day-long slowdown for 'too many requests' only. It amends a promise you agreed, so it's yours.
asks.whyYours: It changes how the app behaves after a storm and amends a promise you agreed (AD3), so it is a product call.

options.says: Wait as asked, then go back to the usual pace; only home's 'too many requests' slows the phone for a day
options.unblocks: the AD3 amendment and its HERD story PR

options.says: Keep it as it is: an overload slows the phone for a day, like 'too many requests'
options.unblocks: nothing; the ask closes and AD3 stands

asks.question: Are the fillers you hear in your interview transcripts?
asks.said: Listen to one or two of your week forty-seven interview answers beside their transcripts. If the ums and ers you hear are there, the essay can state filler counts plainly. If some are missing, counts stay 'at least'. If many are missing, home tries a stronger verbatim setting. Only you can hear that.
asks.whyYours: Only you can hear your own takes and judge whether the transcript caught what you said.

options.says: Yes, they're there: say the count plainly
options.unblocks: The essay states filler counts as they are

options.says: Some are missing: keep saying 'at least'
Many are missing: try a stronger verbatim setting
options.unblocks: A small server change to how home transcribes interview takes, then check again

asks.question: Should Korean practice be set in one shared drama world?
asks.said: Korean practice could be one shared drama world where every scene stands alone, like a sitcom; scenes with no shared cast, as today; or a series that continues. It decides how practice feels to come back to. The recommendation is the shared world, and it unblocks building and playing scenes in it.
asks.whyYours: It decides what the drama is and how it feels to come back to: a product call about your own practice.

options.says: One shared world, every scene stands alone (a sitcom)
options.unblocks: KP6 and KP8, which build and play scenes in it

options.says: Each scene self-contained, with no shared cast, as today
options.unblocks: KP6 without a bible; scenes don't share characters

options.says: A series in order, with episodes that continue
options.unblocks: KP6 with episodes, but sessions are no longer memoryless

asks.question: May clips cut from shows, songs and podcasts be kept on home for your practice?
asks.said: Korean practice could keep short clips from shows, songs and podcasts on home, for you alone, never shared. It's about other people's work and what risk you'll take with it. Yes gives the richest native audio; no keeps practice to pointers, open-licence and made-for-us recordings.
asks.whyYours: It's a question of what risk you're willing to take with other people's work, not a code call.

options.says: Yes, kept on home only, never shared or published
options.unblocks: KP7's private cuts: the richest native audio, including drama delivery

options.says: No: pointers, notes, open-licence and made-for-us recordings only
options.unblocks: KP7 without private cuts; native spans come mostly from YouTube and recordings

asks.question: When TOPIK keeps your level, how should the Show level filter treat it?
asks.said: TOPIK can keep your level across reloads, but the Show level filter is the only thing that sets it, so one look would hold that level for good. The recommendation is that the filter remembers it and All lets go. Whether a look counts as a choice is yours.
asks.whyYours: Only the Show level filter sets the level today, so one tap to look would hold that level for good. Whether a look counts as a choice is your call.

options.says: The filter remembers it, and All lets go of it
Only an explicit level choice is kept
options.unblocks: #2612 lands after a level control of its own is added

options.says: Keep it as it is, and say so in the store's words

asks.question: Pin every GitHub Action to a commit, or keep version tags?
asks.said: The workflows could pin every GitHub Action to a commit, with Dependabot moving the pins, or keep version tags and record why. It trades supply-chain risk against upkeep, and the repositories are yours to keep.
asks.whyYours: It trades a supply-chain risk against how much upkeep the workflows take, and the repos are yours to keep.

options.says: Pin every action to a commit; Dependabot moves the pins
options.unblocks: U8 opens with every unpinned finding cleared

options.says: Keep version tags, and record why in zizmor's config
options.unblocks: U8 opens with the finding set aside, and a reason
